correctness.rationale: Direct derivation of the characteristic polynomial and the three Jury inequalities gives Schur stability. For nonnegative coefficients positivity is inductive; in the remaining interval the exact real-root decomposition shows negativity at one parity unless the negative-root coefficient vanishes. Exact rational Taylor intervals prove the required finite signs; convexity of exp(s) F" gives a unique inflection of F, and its derivative signs imply exactly two simple roots. The exact first-negative index formulas prove the inverse-linear onset and logarithmic resonance delays. The included checker replays all signs and 2557 finite numerical comparisons; those computations are not substituted for the infinite proof. The theorem explicitly excludes unrounded coefficients and corrected iteration.

value.rationale: Stability of a parareal coarse integrator does not imply preservation of positive scalar decays. For the optimized 2026 O2CP, the theorem supplies the sharp all-time safe spectral range, proves generic failure beyond it, identifies exactly two isolated nonrobust exceptions caused by exact fine/coarse matching, and quantifies inverse-linear and logarithmic delays hiding negative values in finite tests. This answers a natural qualitative design constraint not controlled by a small parareal error factor. It is a restricted, exact self-contained fact; no wider PDE maximum-principle or general parareal failure is claimed.
